title: Billionaire Ray Dalio Says an AI-Fueled $4.4 Trillion Debt Crisis Is Coming
source_used: 24/7 Wall St., read on Yahoo Finance
key_facts: Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio wrote a LinkedIn post on Tuesday titled 'The Numbers Behind the Bond Bear Market'.
He projects annual net US debt supply will reach about $4.4 trillion in 2027, up from $3.5 trillion in 2025, roughly a 26% increase.
The figure covers borrowing across the economy, not AI debt alone, and excludes refinancing of existing debt.
Dalio separately estimates corporations will need about $2 trillion to refinance debt in 2027, alongside $1.4 trillion in new borrowing.
He puts hyperscaler bond issuance at about $220 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with $108 billion in all of 2025.
The article, citing Reuters, says hyperscalers now account for 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, against less than 1% in 2024.
The article says Dalio describes a financing squeeze that could develop, rather than an inevitable crash.
quote_evidence: In a post on Tuesday over at LinkedIn, "The Numbers Behind the Bond Bear Market," Dalio projects annual net U.S. debt supply will reach approximately $4.4 trillion in 2027, up from $3.5 trillion in 2025.
The figure covers borrowing across the economy, not AI debt alone.
His analysis deserves attention, although they describe a financing squeeze that could develop, rather than an inevitable crash.
why_it_matters_hint: More borrowing competing for the same lenders could raise financing costs for AI builders, but the figure covers the whole economy and is a projection.
notes: Read on Yahoo Finance, which carries 24/7 Wall St.'s text (with advertising for stock-picking reports, ignored). The pool headline 'AI-Fueled $4.4 Trillion Debt Crisis Is Coming' overstates the article: the figure is whole-economy borrowing and the article itself says 'rather than an inevitable crash'. The post is dated Tuesday 13 Oct, before the window.
